A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a [[Definition:Metric Space|metric space]].
Then:
:$\forall x, y, z \in M: \size {\map d {x, z} - \map d {y, z} } \le \map d {x, y}$

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a [[Definition:Metric Space|metric space]].
Then:
:$\forall x, y, z \in M: \map d {x, z} \le \map d {x, y} + \map d {y, z}$

substitutions.the triple (x,z) via y: both orderings: d(x,z) via y and d(y,z) via x

validity_conditions: Applying the triangle inequality to d(x,z) gives d(x,z) - d(y,z) <= d(x,y).
Applying it to d(y,z) (and symmetry d(x,y)=d(y,x)) gives d(y,z) - d(x,z) <= d(x,y).
Two bounds -c <= v <= c combine to |v| <= c with v = d(x,z)-d(y,z).
proof_plan:
From the [[Definition:Metric Space Axioms|triangle inequality]]:
:$\map d {x, z} - \map d {y, z} \le \map d {x, y}$

Exchanging the roles of $x$ and $y$, and using [[Definition:Symmetric Relation|symmetry]] of $d$:
:$\map d {y, z} - \map d {x, z} \le \map d {y, x} = \map d {x, y}$

Combining:
:$-\map d {x, y} \le \map d {x, z} - \map d {y, z} \le \map d {x, y}$
